system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: As of August 2026, what wording does Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code use to define the limits of punishing a child? Quote the wording of the provision as currently in force, in full.
raw_response:
The applicable provision is **Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code**. As currently in force, it allows a person exercising parental power to discipline a child only within stated limits.

**Section 1567(2)** reads, in full:

> “(2) to admonish or punish the child as appropriate for the purpose of educating, instructing or modifying the child’s behaviour; provided that this must not be done by maltreatment or by any method involving violence against the body or mind of the child.”

This is a translation of the current Thai text; the legally authoritative text is the Thai-language version.
